Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is preparing the SIG/CAIQ follow-up and we have a couple of targeted asks around encryption and key management before we close the risk review:

1) Rotation cadence and evidence: please confirm the standard rotation windows for root KEKs and tenant wrapping keys when using Redwood Private with HSM-backed keys. For audit purposes we need an example rotation schedule and a sample signed HSM attestation page showing the operator and timestamp.

2) Cross-region wrapping: do you perform cross-region KEK wrapping for DR? If so, what evidence do you provide that keys were wrapped/unwrapped (log format, retention)? We need a short explanation and a sample log extract.

3) In-transit encryption and cipher suites: SIG asks for supported TLS versions and cipher suites for service-to-service traffic, and whether you support mutual TLS for customer-managed deployments.

Can you provide a consolidated packet we can attach to the SIG response (one zip with rotation timeline, attestation PDF, and a scrubbed log sample)? We are on a tight deadline for the CAIQ closing this week.

Appreciate a short response with artifacts or expected delivery time.

Best,
Elena Morales

Adding two quick clarifications to Ben's summary for the packet to Northpine:

1) Cipher suites & mTLS: internal service-to-service uses TLS1.3 by default, with the following permitted ciphers: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256. For customer-managed Redwood Private we support mutual TLS endpoints for the control plane and can configure client cert validation.

2) Retention & legal hold: our archive for wrap/unwrap logs is chain-hashed and retained 2 years by default; we have a standard process for legal hold requests that extends retention and issues a signed snapshot. For customers requiring longer retention we can enable 5-year retention via contract amendment.

3) For the cross-region example log, I'll add an explicit DR drill marker so auditors can see wrap -> transfer -> unwrap sequence.

Jonas Weber
Principal Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference
